question.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(X<x)=P(Z<\frac{x-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =1$ and $\sigma =3.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<2.65) & =P(Z<\frac{2.65-1}{3}) \\  & =P(Z<0.55) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.55) \\  & =Φ(0.55)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14263116/assets/155088a94114351eb8c2cc110efbf46b1820c7fa2ad5bb2677922f905d0bd286.png)

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.55)=0.7088.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(X<2.65)=0.7088.
$$
